items.promptText: How much of the offer is gift aid — money that is neither earned by working nor repaid?
What do all four aid lines total?
What gap remains between the cost of attendance and the total aid offered?
What percentage of the cost of attendance is covered by gift aid? Round to one decimal place.
If work study is not counted as aid — because it must be worked for — what is the effective gap?
Which single line of this offer will still be owed after the year is over?

Verification: $7,300 of gift aid against $21,400 of cost is 0.34112, or 34.1%. t2-p2: If work study is not counted as aid — because it must be worked for — what is the effective gap? Answer: $10,600.00. Verification: The $8,400 gap plus the $2,200 the applicant must earn rather than receive. t2-p3: Which single line of this offer will still be owed after the year is over? Answer: The $3,500 subsidised loan. Verification: Grants and scholarships are not repaid and work study is wages for hours worked; only the loan creates an obligation that outlasts the year.
